tagline: From Cumberland Gap over the plateau to where the rivers meet.
intro: The east end leaves US 25E just south of Cumberland Gap on Powell Valley Road, with the Powell River on one hand and the escarpment of the Cumberland Plateau standing a thousand feet or more on the other. A short run on I-75 passes the rock ribs called the Devil's Racetrack, and then TN 63 climbs for 21 miles through the jumbled peaks of the Cumberland Mountains.

On top the land opens into a wide, rolling tableland, past an English colony at Rugby and a German settlement at Allardt. Beyond Jamestown the road comes down by degrees into the farmland of the Wolf River valley and runs on west to the Cumberland.

moments.title: Rugby
moments.text: Thomas Hughes founded the colony in 1880 for the idle second sons of the English gentry, who found the plateau soil wanted more manual labor than they were used to.

moments.title: Alvin York farm and gristmill
moments.text: Nashville's Rotary Club gave Alvin York this Wolf River farm in 1922, after he came home with the Medal of Honor and turned down most offers to profit from it.

moments.title: Celina
moments.text: The byway ends in an old steamboat town where the Obey meets the Cumberland, and where logs cut in the forests upstream once came down to be rafted on to Nashville.
